Core concepts

Body parsing

Parse JSON, form, text and raw request bodies into req.body with size limits and content-type gating.

The four parsers#

routiva ships four body parsers, all built on one streaming reader:

  • json() for application/json
  • urlencoded() for application/x-www-form-urlencoded
  • text() for text/plain
  • raw() for a Buffer of anything

Each one writes a parsed value to req.body and shares the same size-limit and error semantics, so you can stack them and let each parser decide whether the request is its job.

js
import { App, json, urlencoded, text, raw } from 'routiva';

const app = new App();

app.use(json({ limit: '1mb' }));
app.use(urlencoded({ extended: true }));
app.use(text());
app.use(raw());

App.json(), App.urlencoded(), App.text() and App.raw() are the same functions attached to the App class.

How a parser decides to run#

Every parser runs the same three checks before touching the stream:

  1. Already parsed? If req.body !== undefined, it calls next() without reading. This is what makes stacking safe — the first parser that handles the request wins and the rest become no-ops.
  2. Is there a body? A request has one when transfer-encoding is present, or content-length is present and greater than 0. A plain GET is skipped.
  3. Does the content type match? The request's content-type is compared to the parser's expected type with a case-insensitive substring match, so application/json; charset=utf-8 matches application/json.

If any check fails the parser calls next() and leaves req.body as undefined.

Gating is a substring match, not a media-type parse. application/vnd.api+json does not contain the string application/json, so the default json() parser skips it. Pass { type: 'application/vnd.api+json' }, or use text()/raw() for those.

json()#

js
app.post('/users', json({ limit: '100kb' }), (req, res) => {
  res.status(201).json(req.body);
});
OptionDefaultBehaviour
limit'1mb'Maximum body size; overflow rejects with 413
type'application/json'Content-Type substring to match
stricttrueBody must start with { or [
reviverundefinedPassed straight to JSON.parse
verifyundefinedCalled as verify(req, res, buffer, 'utf-8') before parsing

Behaviour worth knowing:

  • An empty body sets req.body = {} instead of leaving it undefined.
  • With the default strict: true, a bare 42, "hello" or true is rejected before parsing. Set strict: false to accept any valid JSON value.
  • Malformed JSON rejects with an HttpError(400) whose type is entity.parse.failed and whose body property holds the raw text.
  • Oversized bodies reject with an HttpError(413) with type: 'entity.too.large' and the message Request entity too large.
  • verify runs after the strict check and before JSON.parse. Because it runs inside the read promise, throwing from verify routes into your error middleware — exactly what a webhook signature check needs.

verify and webhook signatures#

verify gets the raw buffer, so it can validate a signature over the exact bytes the client sent, before any JSON transformation:

js
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
import { HttpError, json } from 'routiva';

app.post('/webhooks/stripe', json({
  verify(req, res, buffer) {
    const expected = createHmac('sha256', SECRET).update(buffer).digest('hex');
    const received = req.header('x-signature') || '';
    const a = Buffer.from(expected);
    const b = Buffer.from(received);
    if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) {
      throw new HttpError(400, 'invalid signature', { type: 'signature.invalid' });
    }
  },
}), (req, res) => {
  res.json({ received: true });
});

urlencoded()#

js
app.use(urlencoded({ extended: true }));
OptionDefaultBehaviour
limit'100kb'Maximum body size
extendedfalseDecode bracket notation into nested objects

urlencoded() has no type option — it always matches application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The body is read with URLSearchParams, so + and percent-escapes are decoded for you.

With the default extended: false, keys stay flat and the last value wins:

text
name=ada&role=admin&role=user    ->    { name: 'ada', role: 'user' }

With extended: true, bracket notation builds nested objects:

text
user[name]=ada&user[address][city]=london

->  { user: { name: 'ada', address: { city: 'london' } } }

The extended parser builds objects only. Array notation such as tags[]=a&tags[]=b stores a key literally named '', not an array. Send JSON when you need arrays.

text()#

js
app.post('/notes', text({ type: 'text/plain' }), (req, res) => {
  res.json({ length: req.body.length });
});
OptionDefaultBehaviour
limit'100kb'Maximum body size
type'text/plain'Content-Type substring to match
encoding'utf8'Passed to buffer.toString(encoding)

req.body is a string. Pass a broader type to accept other text-ish content types.

raw()#

js
app.post('/upload', raw({ type: 'application/octet-stream', limit: '5mb' }), (req, res) => {
  res.json({ bytes: req.body.length });
});
OptionDefaultBehaviour
limit'100kb'Maximum body size
typeunsetWhen omitted, every content type is accepted; when set, it must match

req.body is a Buffer. Unlike the other three parsers, raw() does not gate on content type unless you pass type, which makes it the catch-all parser to register last.

Size limits#

Limits are parsed by parseBytes, which understands bare numbers and unit suffixes:

ValueBytes
10241,024
'100kb'102,400
'1mb'1,048,576
'2gb'2,147,483,648

When the accumulated size exceeds the limit, the reader stops collecting chunks, drains the rest of the stream with stream.resume() so the socket stays writable, and rejects with a 413. An unparsable limit falls back to that parser's default.

What the client sees#

Body-parser errors are HttpErrors, so the default error handler renders them as JSON:

SituationStatustypeDefault message
Malformed JSON400entity.parse.failedthe JSON.parse error message
Non-object/array under strict400entity.parse.failedJSON body must be an object or array
Body over limit413entity.too.largeRequest entity too large

Because 4xx errors are exposed (status < 500), their message reaches the client. Override the shape with your own error middleware — see Error handling.
